Let $U,V,a,b$ satisfy [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]]. **Inputs:** an integer $M\ge2$, images $R_0=a,R_1,\ldots,R_M=b$ in $U$, spring constant $\kappa\ge0$, fixed step $\eta>0$, force and spacing tolerances $\tau_F,\tau_s\ge0$, an ordinary-step count $n_{\rm climb}\in\mathbb N_0$, and a finite update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$. Require $n_{\rm climb}\le N$. **Output:** the last chain and one of `tolerances-met`, `tangent-failure`, `geometry-failure`, `nonfinite-evaluation`, or `budget-exhausted`.

At each iteration, endpoints are fixed and only interior images are updated. For $i=1,\ldots,M-1$, write $\Delta_i^+=R_{i+1}-R_i$, $\Delta_i^-=R_i-R_{i-1}$, and $V_i=V(R_i)$. Select an unnormalized tangent by

$$\tau_i=\begin{cases}\Delta_i^+,&V_{i+1}>V_i>V_{i-1},\\\Delta_i^-,&V_{i+1}<V_i<V_{i-1},\\w_{\max}\Delta_i^+ + w_{\min}\Delta_i^-,&\text{otherwise and }V_{i+1}>V_{i-1},\\w_{\min}\Delta_i^+ + w_{\max}\Delta_i^-,&\text{otherwise and }V_{i+1}<V_{i-1},\\\Delta_i^++\Delta_i^-,&V_{i+1}=V_{i-1},\end{cases}$$

where $w_{\max}=\max(|V_{i+1}-V_i|,|V_{i-1}-V_i|)$ and $w_{\min}=\min(|V_{i+1}-V_i|,|V_{i-1}-V_i|)$. If $\tau_i=0$, return `tangent-failure`; otherwise set $t_i=\tau_i/\|\tau_i\|_2$. Nonfinite energies, gradients, or forces return `nonfinite-evaluation`.

Initialize the update counter $k=0$. At iteration $k$, use the ordinary force

$$F_i=-(I-t_it_i^T)\nabla V(R_i)+\kappa(\|\Delta_i^+\|_2-\|\Delta_i^-\|_2)t_i.$$

When $k\ge n_{\rm climb}$, choose the least index $i_*$ attaining the largest interior energy and replace that image's force by

$$F_{i_*}^{\rm CI}=-\nabla V(R_{i_*})+2(\nabla V(R_{i_*})^Tt_{i_*})t_{i_*};$$

the climbing image has no spring force. The remaining interior images retain the ordinary force. Thus iterations $k=0,\ldots,n_{\rm climb}-1$ use ordinary forces and the first climbing force is evaluated at iteration $k=n_{\rm climb}$. At each iteration report the maximum force norm and spacing residual $\max_i|\|\Delta_i^+\|_2-\|\Delta_i^-\|_2|$. Stop with `tolerances-met` only if both are within their declared tolerances. If a tolerance fails and $k=N$, return `budget-exhausted`; only when $k<N$ update every interior image by $R_i^{k+1}=R_i^k+\eta F_i^k$. Leaving $U$ returns `geometry-failure`. After a valid update set $k\leftarrow k+1$ and repeat. The tolerance check precedes the budget check, so $N=0$ still checks the initial chain and $n_{\rm climb}=N$ uses a climbing force at the final residual check (without an update if the budget is then exhausted).

The finite stopping status does not assert convergence to a MEP, a saddle, or a continuum path.

Return the last point, direction, reported residuals, and a status from `force-tolerance`, `mode-unverified`, `rotation-cap`, `translation-cap`, `geometry-failure`, `rotation-failure`, or `nonfinite-evaluation`.

Initialize the translation-update counter $k=0$, the current point $x=x_0$, and the current unit direction $v=v_0$. At each translation iteration, start with the current $v$, set the rotation-update counter $j=0$, and repeat the following residual test and possible update:

1. If $x\pm\epsilon v\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`. Evaluate approximate gradients $\widehat g_\pm$ at $x\pm\epsilon v$ with the declared error bound, and form $D_\epsilon=(\widehat g_+-\widehat g_-)/(2\epsilon)$. Nonfinite data return `nonfinite-evaluation`.
2. Set $r_{\rm rot}=\|(I-vv^T)D_\epsilon\|_2$. If $r_{\rm rot}\le\tau_{\rm rot}$, end this rotation loop. If the test fails and $j=J$, return `rotation-cap` with the last direction. Otherwise set $w=v-\alpha(I-vv^T)D_\epsilon$. If $w=0$, return `rotation-failure`; else replace $v$ by $w/\|w\|_2$, set $j\leftarrow j+1$, and repeat the rotation test.

Thus $J$ counts direction updates, and the current direction is tested before the cap is returned, including when $J=0$. A small rotational residual by itself does not certify that the direction is the lowest eigenmode. If no validated spectral-gap or mode-tracking certificate is supplied, label the mode status `mode-unverified`.

After a rotation residual passes, evaluate $\widehat g(x)$ with error at most $\eta$. If it is nonfinite, return `nonfinite-evaluation`. If $\|\widehat g(x)\|_2\le\tau_F$, return `force-tolerance` together with the mode status. If $k=K$, return `translation-cap`; perform an update only when $k<K$.

$$x^+=x+\sigma\bigl[-\widehat g(x)+2(\widehat g(x)^Tv)v\bigr].$$

If $x^+\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`; otherwise set $x\leftarrow x^+$, set $k\leftarrow k+1$, and begin the next translation iteration. Thus $K$ counts translation updates; the force-tolerance test is made before the cap test, including when $K=0$. This finite procedure makes no arbitrary-start, termination, saddle-convergence, or global-transition claim.

Require every residual $\|H(x_k)q_j-\widehat\lambda_jq_j\|_2\le\tau_{\rm eig}$, $\sqrt d\,\tau_{\rm eig}\le\gamma/2$, and $\widehat\lambda_j\in I_j$. The Hessian $H=\nabla^2V$ is symmetric by [[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]].

For $k=0,\ldots,N$, in order:

1. If $x_k\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`. If $x_k\notin B_2(x_{\rm ref},r_{\rm loc})$, return `outside-local-basin`. Compute $g_k=\nabla V(x_k)$. If $\|g_k\|_2\le\tau_g$, return `gradient-residual-tolerance`; if $k=N$, return `budget-exhausted`.
2. If an eigenpair residual exceeds $\tau_{\rm eig}$, $\sqrt d\tau_{\rm eig}>\gamma/2$, or some $\widehat\lambda_j\notin I_j$, return `eigensolve-tolerance-failure`. If the validated intervals do not satisfy $u_1\le-\gamma$ and $\ell_j\ge\gamma$ for all $j\ge2$ (with the dimension-one convention in the definition), return `index-one-branch-failure`. If $|q_1^Tv_{\rm ref}|<\tau_{\rm mode}$, return `mode-tracking-failure`; otherwise replace $q_1$ by its sign-aligned representative with $q_1^Tv_{\rm ref}\ge0$ and use this as the next mode reference. This overlap check detects a mode-branch change but does not alter the Newton correction.
3. Call [[alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals]] with $A=H(x_k)$ and $r=g_k$. If its Jacobian is singular, return `singular-hessian`. Its correction $p_k$ is the exact Newton solution of $H(x_k)p_k=-g_k$ in the mathematical model; the eigenpair data certifies the index-one branch but does not replace this linear solve.
4. If $x_k+p_k\notin U$ or lies outside $B_2(x_{\rm ref},r_{\rm loc})$, return `outside-local-basin`. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k$ and continue.

Actual Statement clause: Let $N\ge2$ and $x_j=2\pi j/N$. If integers $k,r$ satisfy $k\equiv r\pmod N$, then
$$
e^{ikx_j}=e^{irx_j}\qquad(0\le j<N).
$$
Consequently, sampling a product of Fourier modes with frequencies $k_1,\ldots,k_s$ gives the same nodal data as the single mode whose frequency is the sum $\sum_{\ell=1}^s k_\ell$ reduced modulo $N$.

The frequency space in [[def-periodic-fourier-collocation-grid]] is real-valued. For complex data, let $\mathcal T_N^{\mathbb C}$ be the space obtained by allowing complex coefficients in that same real basis, and extend its cardinal formula by
$$
I_N^{\mathbb C}V(x):=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}V_jL_j(x),\qquad V\in\mathbb C^N.
$$
Then $I_N^{\mathbb C}V$ is the unique member of $\mathcal T_N^{\mathbb C}$ with nodal data $V$. On real data this formula agrees with $I_N$; in the even case the complex Nyquist samples are interpolated by the real basis function $\cos(Nx/2)$.

additional_source_clauses.text:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

proofparagraphs.text: By [F1], $u-\Pi_Nu=\sum_{n>N}c_nT_n$. Orthogonality from [F2] gives $\|u-\Pi_Nu\|_C^2=\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_{n>N}|c_n|^2.$ Since $n>N$ implies $(1+n^2)^s\ge(1+(N+1)^2)^s$, this is at most $(1+(N+1)^2)^{-s}\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_{n>N}(1+n^2)^s|c_n|^2 \le(1+(N+1)^2)^{-s}\|u\|_{H_C^s}^2.$ Taking square roots proves the result for finite sums. [F1, F2, algebra]

Finite sums are dense in the completion defining $H_C^s$. The truncation $\Pi_N$ is a contraction in the coefficient norm and in the $C$-norm, so both sides of the finite-sum inequality pass to the limit along any Cauchy sequence of finite sums. This yields the stated estimate for every $u\in H_C^s$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
